title: Anthropic update on independent evaluators
gist: Anthropic is embedding METR staff with employee-like access, with publication rights it cannot veto, and is building a three-tier evaluator access model with SecureBio, Accenture and Faculty, positioning this as bank-examiner-style oversight that every frontier lab should adopt.

insights.claim: Anthropic has onboarded six METR employees with company hardware, office space and internal-tool access roughly on par with its own risk-assessment teams, and METR will publish its analysis of Anthropic's risk levels and practices.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Frontier-lab safety oversight is moving from voluntary reports to embedded audit, a precursor to regulatory norms.
insights.locator: What we mean by employee-like access

insights.claim: Anthropic cannot veto METR publications; it can only require redaction in narrow categories such as customer data, privileged information, and model architecture, and METR may publicly say whether it thinks redactions were justified.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Real publication independence makes evaluator findings a credible signal on lab risk posture.
insights.locator: What we mean by employee-like access

insights.claim: Anthropic draws an analogy to bank supervision, where regulators place resident examiners inside the largest banks because firms know more about their own risk than outsiders do.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Suggests the likely regulatory template for frontier AI is resident-examiner supervision of systemically important labs.
insights.quote: Although the analogy isn’t exact, bank supervision operates on similar logic.
insights.locator: Why we work with independent evaluators

insights.claim: Anthropic is developing three tiers of evaluator access: narrowly scoped investigations with publication needing Anthropic approval, then tier two with publication without approval and more information, then tier three employee-like access as with METR.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Watch which evaluators graduate to higher tiers as a measure of how real lab-transparency commitments are.

insights.claim: SecureBio is reviewing the chemical and biological weapons chapter of Anthropic's August Risk Report after a published pilot review of the previous report, and Accenture and Faculty are partnering on red-teaming, alignment assessments and safeguard testing.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Large consultancies entering AI assurance signals a growing paid AI-audit services market.

insights.claim: Anthropic signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, in which companies pledged to partner with independent external auditors, and states every frontier AI company should embed evaluators voluntarily.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Independent-audit commitments are becoming an industry and policy norm that competitors will be pressed to match.
insights.quote: We’re embedding evaluators voluntarily, and we believe every frontier AI company should do the same.

top_entities: White House Accord on Super Intelligence
